instructions: Grate the carrot and half the cucumber. Finely chop half the onion. Chop 4 tbsp of the dill and 2 tbsp of the cilantro. Finely chop the ginger and a few of the curry leaves.
In a large bowl, mix the rice flour with the carrot, cucumber, onion, dill, cilantro, ginger, curry leaves, cumin seeds and salt.
Squeeze the vegetables into the flour with your hands for about 1 minute, until the flour looks damp.
Add warm water a few tablespoons at a time, mixing, until it comes together into a soft dough that doesn't crack when you press it.
Heat a flat skillet or tawa over medium heat. Cut a sheet of parchment paper about 8 inches square and brush it with oil.
Divide the dough into 10 balls. Put one on the oiled parchment. With oiled fingers, pat it into a thin round about 6 inches across.
Flip the parchment over so the roti sits on the hot pan, and press it lightly. Cook for about 20 seconds, then peel the parchment off slowly.
Drizzle about 1/2 tsp oil around the edge. Cook for 2 minutes, until the underside has golden spots.
Flip and cook the other side for 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer it to a plate.
Shape the next roti while the one in the pan cooks. Repeat with the rest of the dough to make 10 in all.
Serve hot with the coconut chutney.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen leads (5 stars from 443): rice flour kneaded with grated carrot and cucumber, onion, dill, cilantro, ginger, curry leaves and cumin, patted thin on oiled paper and roasted on a hot pan. My Cooking Journey (4.95 from 20) uses carrot and onion only, plain water and a parchment sheet. Hebbar's three green chilies are left out of the dough to keep it mild. Ten rotis one at a time take about 40 minutes all in, longer than a 30 minute breakfast; a second pan speeds it up.
